cues.say: Component 19: Flags and kill switches. Settings you flip while the site runs, with no code release. A kill switch is a flag for emergencies. You'll bring this up during go-live prep.
Think of it as: Light switches you install before the party. Use it for pause orders, waiting room on, hide photos, and close a slot.
Here's a real scenario. 4:10 PM on game day: payment errors spike.
Without it: Write code, review, release, mid-incident.
With it: Flip pause new orders.
Seconds later the button says paused for a few minutes.
Paid orders keep flowing; flip back at 4:25.
Database busy later? Flip hide photos.
Why it works: A switch takes seconds, and each one was tested the day before.
In the interview, say: Every switch is tested on game day.
A few related terms you may hear.
Feature flag: Turns a feature on or off at runtime.
Graceful degradation: Turn off extras so the core keeps working.
Load shedding: Reject some requests instantly so the rest stay fast.
